intro: Miami rewards visitors with beaches, Cuban food, art deco streets and lively nightlife. Pick how long you have and what you enjoy most.
tour_note: Check the tour page for which entry tickets are included.

notes: Metrorail runs elevated trains to downtown, the airport and Dadeland; fare about $2.25.
Metromover is free and links downtown and Brickell.
Metrobus covers the county; route S runs downtown to Miami Beach.
Taxis are metered and pricey; Uber and Lyft work well.
Driving is common but traffic and parking are hard; walking is best in dense areas.
Tri-Rail commuter trains link Miami, Fort Lauderdale and West Palm Beach.

south-beach.name: South Beach
south-beach.price_text: Free to enter; parking and sun loungers cost extra
south-beach.hours: Beach open 24 hours; lifeguards usually 09:00–17:00, check on the day
south-beach.tip: Come early morning for space and cooler sand. Swim near a lifeguard stand.

art-deco.name: Art Deco Historic District
art-deco.price_text: Free to walk; guided tours around USD 30–40
art-deco.hours: Streets always open; many buildings are hotels you can enter in the lobby
art-deco.tip: Walk Ocean Drive from 5th to 15th Street. Look up at the pastel facades and neon signs.

miami-beach.name: Miami Beach
miami-beach.price_text: Free; parking garages charge by the hour
miami-beach.hours: Beach open 24 hours; lifeguards daytime only
miami-beach.tip: The beach is long. North of South Beach is quieter and less crowded.

wynwood-walls.name: Wynwood Walls
wynwood-walls.price_text: Around USD 12–18 adult; check current price online
wynwood-walls.hours: Usually daily late morning to evening; hours change, check on the day
wynwood-walls.tip: Buy tickets online to skip the line. The surrounding streets have free murals too.

vizcaya.name: Vizcaya Museum and Gardens
vizcaya.price_text: Around USD 20–30 adult; discounts for children and students
vizcaya.hours: Usually Wed–Mon 09:30–16:30, closed some days; check on the day
vizcaya.tip: Go early for cooler gardens. The waterfront terrace is the best photo spot.

millionaires-row-cruise.name: Millionaire's Row Cruise
millionaires-row-cruise.price_text: Around USD 30–45 for a 90-minute boat tour
millionaires-row-cruise.hours: Several departures daily, roughly 10:00–20:00; check on the day
millionaires-row-cruise.tip: Sit on the open upper deck. Sunset departures show the skyline at its best.

american-dream.name: American Dream Miami
american-dream.price_text: Prices vary by attraction; check the official site before you go
american-dream.hours: Check on the day; large malls usually open late morning to evening
american-dream.tip: This is a big indoor mall and entertainment complex. Plan a half day and book rides ahead.

burger-king.name: Burger King
burger-king.hours: Most branches open long hours daily; check on the day
burger-king.tip: Fast and cheap. Good for a quick lunch between sights.

popeyes.name: Popeyes
popeyes.hours: Most branches open long hours daily; check on the day
popeyes.tip: Fried chicken and biscuits. Expect a short wait at busy times.

santas-enchanted-forest.name: Santa's Enchanted Forest
santas-enchanted-forest.price_text: Ticket prices vary; check the official site
santas-enchanted-forest.hours: Seasonal, usually evenings in the holiday season; check on the day
santas-enchanted-forest.tip: A seasonal holiday fair with rides and lights. Go on a weekday for shorter lines.

zoo-miami.name: Zoo Miami
zoo-miami.hours: Usually daily 10:00–17:00; check on the day
zoo-miami.tip: It is large and hot. Bring water, sunscreen and plan to rent a bike or tram.

lincoln-road.name: Lincoln Road Mall
lincoln-road.hours: Pedestrian street always open; shops and cafes set their own hours
lincoln-road.tip: A pedestrian shopping street for people-watching and a coffee. Good evening stroll.

espanola-way.name: Española Way
espanola-way.price_text: Free to walk; restaurants charge their own prices
espanola-way.hours: Street always open; restaurants usually lunch to late evening
espanola-way.tip: A short historic street with cafes. Walk it at dusk for the lights.

bayside-marketplace.name: Bayside Marketplace
bayside-marketplace.price_text: Free to enter; food and boat tours cost extra
bayside-marketplace.hours: Usually daily late morning to late evening; check on the day
bayside-marketplace.tip: Waterfront market with food stalls. Many boat tours leave from here.

little-havana-walk.name: Little Havana (Calle Ocho)
little-havana-walk.price_text: Free to walk; food and drinks cost extra
little-havana-walk.hours: Streets always open; cafes and shops daytime to evening
little-havana-walk.tip: Walk Calle Ocho for cigar shops and Cuban coffee. Try a small espresso at a ventanita.

coconut-grove-walk.name: Coconut Grove waterfront walk
coconut-grove-walk.hours: Parks usually sunrise to sunset; check on the day
coconut-grove-walk.tip: Shady streets and a small marina. A calm break from the beach crowds.

everglades-airboat.name: Everglades airboat tour
everglades-airboat.price_text: Around USD 30–60 depending on tour length
everglades-airboat.hours: Departures daytime daily; check on the day
everglades-airboat.tip: Book ahead and bring sun protection. Ask if hotel pickup is included.

south-pointe-park.name: South Pointe Park
south-pointe-park.hours: Usually open daily early to late; check on the day
south-pointe-park.tip: Best free viewpoint of the cruise ships and the skyline. Go at sunset.

perez-art-museum.name: Pérez Art Museum Miami (PAMM)
perez-art-museum.price_text: Around USD 16–20 adult; check current price
perez-art-museum.hours: Usually Tue–Sun late morning to evening, closed some days; check on the day
perez-art-museum.tip: Indoor art with a waterfront terrace. A good rainy-day plan.

ocean-drive.name: Ocean Drive
ocean-drive.price_text: Free to walk; drinks and food cost extra
ocean-drive.hours: Street always open; bars and cafes late into the night
ocean-drive.tip: Walk it once in the evening for the neon. Check menu prices before sitting down.

styles.label: Beach
styles.blurb: South Beach sand, Ocean Drive and warm water swims.

styles.label: Food
styles.blurb: Cuban counters, stone crab and Little Havana cafés.

styles.label: Art
styles.blurb: Wynwood murals, Pérez Art Museum and Design District galleries.

stays.why: Walk to the beach, Ocean Drive and Lincoln Road. Best for first-timers who want sand and nightlife on foot.
Free Metromover, good restaurants and bars, and quick links to the airport. Cheaper than the beach.
Leafy, relaxed streets with cafés and marinas. Quieter base, a short drive from the beach.
Pretty Mediterranean-style streets, good dining and the Biltmore. Calm and walkable in the centre.

food: Try Cuban food: a cubano sandwich, ropa vieja and strong cafecito. Little Havana on SW 8th Street (Calle Ocho) is the classic stop.
Stone crab claws are a Miami specialty, in season roughly October to May. Prices are high; check the day's market price.
Eat at a ventanita (walk-up window) for cheap coffee and snacks, often under $10.
Seafood and Latin dishes along the Miami River and in Brickell; book ahead on weekends.
Food halls and markets are good for groups with mixed tastes. Check opening hours on the day.
more_time: Swap a beach afternoon for the Everglades: an airboat tour from the Tamiami Trail side, about an hour's drive each way.
Art lovers can add a day in Wynwood and the Design District for murals and galleries.
Take a day trip to the Florida Keys or Key Biscayne beaches if you want quieter sand.
